steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat a waffle iron according to manufacturer's instructions.

Whisk eggs in a large bowl until light and fluffy. Add flour, milk, and vegetable oil and mix to combine. Whisk in sugar, then mix in baking powder, salt, and vanilla just until smooth, being careful not to overmix.
Spray the preheated waffle iron with nonstick spray. Pour batter onto the hot waffle iron and cook until golden brown and the iron stops steaming, 3 to 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Waffles
raw_recipe.description: This waffle recipe makes tasty waffles with simple pantry ingredients. Skip the boxed mix and use this batter now or refrigerate for up to a week.

video.description: The waffle recipe in this video is the only one you'll need to make homemade waffles with your waffle iron. Simple pantry ingredients mix up quickly in this easy batter that can be used right away or stored in the refrigerator for up to a week. Serve waffles hot with whipped cream and fresh fruit or with butter and maple syrup for either breakfast, brunch, or a snack.

review.reviewBody: 5+++++ I love this recipe. I made some healthy substitutions and it turned out yummy for me. I used whole wheat flour, splenda, and apple sauce in lieu of the oil. I also added about 1 tsp of brown sugar and 1/2 tsp of cinnamon as others have recommended. I followed another users recommendation to seperate the whites from the eggs (beated until fluffy) and folded them into the batter as the final step--turned out nice and fluffy. I served these plain with the cinnamon butter recipe. Also, you can freeze left-overs (if any) in plastic baggies to be taken out at a later time to be quickly reheated in the toaster. 5-star plus--thanks for the wonderful recipe!

I will never use another waffle recipe again! I put all the ingredients into a blender to mix and baked beautiful, light and crisp waffles. I even used all whole wheat flour, and they were still light and wonderful.

Good recipe, especially because I could make it the night before. I changed it slightly, separating the eggs and whipping the whites until they were light and fluffy before I mixed in the rest of the ingredients. I also doubled the sugar and vanilla, as was suggested, and added a sprinkling of cinnamon and nutmeg. Delicious!

I used this recipe but didn't feel like cleaning my waffle iron so I made pancakes with it, lol. I doubled the vanilla and added a dash of cinnamon.... these were the lightest, fluffiest, and most perfect pancakes I've ever had/ made.

Good recipe with the following tweaks:

- Added 1/2 TB sugar and 1 tsp cinnamon
- Whisked egg whites until very fluffy then folded them into the mixed batter at the end

The result were waffles that were very crisp but light. Certainly there are other recipes that add butter and loads of sugar, and therefore calories, but I wanted a more healthy option and this one was perfect. It made about 12 3"x3" waffles, eight of which are now frozen to be reheated for my daughter. 

All around a very good recipe and one that isn't overly loaded with calorie bloat. I will make them again.

I've made these several times for my family. They always get rave reviews. I follow the recipe very closely, with the exception that usually separate the egg whites and beat them separately, folding them in at the end. Sometimes, if I have buttermilk on hand, I will use that instead of regular milk. Either way, they turn out fabulously every time.

The recipe came together quite easily! We love orange flavored waffles, so I reduced the milk by 3/4 cup and replaced that with orange juice, along with a healthy tablespoon of orange zest. Best waffles we've had in years!

I made these a couple of weeks ago, scaling the recipe to serve 12. I used cake flour (4 1/2 c.), fat-free milk, melted margarine (not oil), doubled the sugar, salt (Kosher) & vanilla. I used 3 T. baking powder. I made the batter the night before which turned out terrific. It made plenty of waffles (corn, blueberry, plain)--enough to freeze or for guests.

These were good. I made the following changes, based on other reviews: (1) whipped the egg whites separately and folded them in at the end and (2) doubled both the sugar and the vanilla. Also, to make them healthier, I used 1 c. all-purpose flour and 1 c. whole wheat flour and 1/4 c. vegetable oil and 1/4 c. unsweetened applesauce. I think it could still use a little more sugar.

Great Recipe and it is the same recipe I’ve been using for years. It came out of a recipe book “Betty Crocker’s 40th Anniversary Cookbook” that I received at my wedding in 1990! Sometimes “Betty” knows best lol. “Betty” suggests using either granulated or brown sugar, whichever you prefer and she also gave the option of using melted butter in place of vegetable oil, which I do and we like it better. We don’t use vegetable oil for anything if we can avoid it. Whip your eggs and fold them in last for the best result. The only change here from the original recipe is the addition of vanilla, which if you’re using Maple Syrup you may not really need. I also add a small amount of cinnamon occasionally for a slight variation. Whole family and extended family always love these waffles. For convenience, measure out your dry ingredients into sandwich bags while you have everything on the counter and have them in your pantry for a quick waffle breakfast any morning! Happy to see the recipe on here! Try it and replace oil with butter, you will be happy you did!

These are absolutely delicious! As others have suggested, I whipped the egg whites and folded them in at the end. I also added a little cinnamon and brown sugar to the mixture which gave it more flavor. I froze the extra waffles and heated them in a toaster a few weeks later and they were yummy! Thanks tor the recipe! No more buying mix at the store! Will definitely make again!

I wound up cutting the recipe in half but leaving the sugar the same. Otherwise they were excellent. Any flaws were due to me trying to use a cast iron waffle iron for the first time. I didn't even know how much batter to put in it. They came out fine although next time I use an electric mixer to beat the eggs.
My go to recipe for waffles

I have made this recipe multiple times. Sometimes I add some colouful sprinkles into the batter. We never, NEVER, have leftovers for the next day for breakfast. My son is a picky eater anf when I make these it is all he eats all day. With Nutella ( I hate this thing). Best recipe ever!
Finally a recipe that actually works well with very little effort
